facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

concepts.why: The patient has a large and deep cutaneous ulcer with necrotic tissue, woody induration of skin, and histopathology showing lobular panniculitis with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates.
The patient has a history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, which is known to cause fibrosis and muscle contracture.
The patient has bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles, which is consistent with muscle contracture.
The patient has a 7-year history of severe mechanical low back pain and elevated serum creatinine kinase, which is consistent with myofascial pain syndrome.

rationales.F03: Meperidine injections are associated with fibrosis and skin lesions
rationales.F04: Cutaneous ulcers are a characteristic feature of Necrotizing Panniculitis
rationales.F05: Woody induration is a common finding in Meperidine-Induced Fibrosis
rationales.F06: Muscle contractures are a common complication of chronic muscle injury
rationales.F11: Lobular panniculitis is a hallmark of Necrotizing Panniculitis

frontier_selector.rationale: Meperidine-Induced Fibrosis best explains the combination of bilateral muscle contractures, restricted range of motion, and history of frequent subcutaneous meperidine injections, with supporting evidence from the patient's self-administration history and the presence of fibrosis in the histopathology report.
